scope: Reviewed every file in research-agent2: src/ (agent loop, tools, web app, render, audit, telemetry, quota, type ID), prompts/system.md, config/agent.yaml, Dockerfile, k8s/deployment.yaml, k8s/networkpolicy.yaml, requirements.txt, README.md. Not found in the repo: .brace/deployment.yaml, CI workflows, CODEOWNERS, tests, Kubernetes RBAC, admission policies, oauth2-proxy config, Fluent Bit and audit index config, SIEM rules, runbooks, and git history (not a git repository). This review reads code only; it does not prove controls work in production. likely_pass items still need the evidence their recipe names. Controls may live outside this repo. A finite review can miss things and does not certify the agent is secure.

evidence.note: Fixed tool map: web_search and fetch_page only; no MCP or dynamic discovery.
Dispatcher denies any tool name not in TOOLS and logs tool_denied.
Task reason given: search the public web and read pages.
Config lists the same two tools, but the harness does not read this list; TOOLS in code is the real allowlist.

findings.summary: Two built-in tools behind a name allowlist enforced in the dispatcher; no MCP servers, shell, or file tools.
findings.next_step: Run recipe B01: export the tool list the running agent sees, call an unlisted tool name and confirm denial. Add a written inventory that also lists the Anthropic and Brave APIs and the /tmp and control mounts with a task reason each.

evidence.note: automountServiceAccountToken: false; no Role or RoleBinding in the repo.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and BRAVE_API_KEY are static API keys; their scope is set at the providers, not in the repo.

findings.summary: No Kubernetes permissions are granted, but the scope of the two provider API keys cannot be read from code.
findings.next_step: Run recipe B02 with the agent's real keys: confirm the Anthropic key is limited to one workspace and the Brave key to search only, and that neither is shared with other services.

evidence.note: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from a Kubernetes Secret: long-lived static key.
BRAVE_API_KEY from the same Secret: long-lived static key.
Key is sent only in a header, not in a prompt (no leak into model context).

findings.summary: Both credentials are fixed API keys with no expiry, rotation job, or secret scanning anywhere in the repo.
findings.next_step: Document a rotation policy and lifetime for both keys, load them from a secrets manager with rotation, add secret scanning in CI, then run recipe B03.

evidence.note: Agent runs as its own ServiceAccount; users never pass their own tokens to it.
User identity is only an email header; no user credential reaches the agent.

findings.summary: Revoking the agent means rotating its two API keys or scaling to zero, which does not touch users, but no cutoff time is stated or measured.
findings.next_step: Set a maximum cutoff time and run the timed drill in recipe B04 (revoke the agent's keys, confirm calls fail while users' other access still works).

evidence.note: fetch_page sends a GET to any model-chosen URL; the URL path and query can carry data out.
Tool runs with no check of target or arguments beyond the tool name.
Egress to 0.0.0.0/0 on 80/443 also reaches cluster-internal services and the cloud metadata address on port 80.
img tags with any http/https src are rendered in the user's browser: a second outbound path with no tool call.

findings.summary: The agent reads untrusted web content, sees the employee's question, and can send data to any URL; untrusted content picks the destination and nothing gates it.
findings.next_step: Record the three capabilities for this agent type. Then either restrict fetch_page to public addresses and an allowlist, or block outbound requests whose URL carries data, and strip external images from the brief. Run recipe B05 with a planted instruction.

evidence.note: No approval mechanism exists in the dispatch path.

findings.summary: No approval system exists; this item is N/A only if B05 is fixed without approvals and that inventory is recorded.
findings.next_step: Resolve B05 first. If outbound fetches are gated by approval, build approval records per recipe B06; otherwise file an N/A for governance with the B05 inventory.

evidence.note: Per-run caps on steps, wall time, tokens enforced by the harness.
Per-run tool-call cap enforced in dispatch.
Per-user daily quota kept in process memory: each of the 2 replicas counts separately and resets on restart.
replicas: 2, so a user gets up to 2x user_daily_runs (100 runs) per day.
Quota is charged before the halt check; no cost cap and no tenant or fleet quota anywhere.

findings.summary: Per-run limits exist, but the per-user quota is per pod and lost on restart, and there is no tenant, fleet, or spend cap.
findings.next_step: Move the user quota to a shared store or gateway, add tenant and fleet spend limits (for example provider spend limits), then run recipe B07 including many concurrent small runs.

evidence.note: ipBlock 0.0.0.0/0 with no except list allows ports 80/443 to every pod, service, and node in the cluster.
Port 80 to 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata) is allowed.
The model chooses the URL, so any internal HTTP service on 80/443 is reachable.

findings.summary: The NetworkPolicy exists but its egress rule does not exclude private, cluster, or metadata ranges, so the agent can reach internal systems.
findings.next_step: Add except: blocks for RFC 1918, cluster CIDRs, 169.254.0.0/16 and IPv6 equivalents, or route egress through an egress proxy; write down every reachable system; run recipe B08.

evidence.note: Egress allowed to 0.0.0.0/0.
follow_redirects=True with no re-check of redirect targets; no DNS pinning; no private-address check.
fetch_page schema accepts any URI.

findings.summary: Egress is open to the whole internet and the fetch tool takes any model-supplied URL and follows redirects unchecked.
findings.next_step: Resolve and pin DNS in fetch_page, reject private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses on every redirect hop, consider an egress proxy, log blocks to a named operator, and run recipe B09.

evidence.note: Image pinned by digest.
Base image pinned by digest.

findings.summary: Images are pinned by digest, but nothing signs them, produces provenance or an SBOM, or verifies them at admission.
findings.next_step: Add a CI build that signs the image and attaches SLSA provenance and an SBOM, and an enforce-mode admission policy for the research namespace; run recipe B10.

evidence.note: Pod meets Pod Security restricted: runAsNonRoot, seccomp RuntimeDefault.
allowPrivilegeEscalation false, readOnlyRootFilesystem true, all capabilities dropped.
Final image is python:3.12-slim, which ships a shell and pip the agent does not need.

findings.summary: The pod security context is strong, but the single-stage image keeps a shell and package manager.
findings.next_step: Use a multi-stage build onto a distroless Python base, add the restricted Pod Security label to the namespace, and run recipe B11.

evidence.note: System prompt is a file in the repo, loaded at start (src/agent.py:16).
Prompt hash feeds the type ID, so a deployed prompt can be linked to source.
No CODEOWNERS, CI, release workflow, or branch protection config in the repo.

findings.summary: Harness and prompt are versioned files, but the repo shows no required review, release pipeline, or force-push protection.
findings.next_step: Add CODEOWNERS for src/, prompts/, config/, k8s/; deploy only from CI on a protected branch; run recipe B12.

evidence.note: Whole response body read with no size or content-type limit.
Full page text returned to the model with no length cap or content check.
Tool output goes straight into the next model request.
Search results are trimmed per field (title 200, snippet 500) - the only size limit.

findings.summary: Fetched pages reach the model with no size, type, or injection check; one large page can exhaust memory or the context window.
findings.next_step: Cap response bytes and output characters in fetch_page, accept only text/html and text/plain, add an injection-pattern check with a hold path, and run recipe R01 with mock pages.

evidence.note: Tool output placed in a tool_result block wrapped in <untrusted_web_content> tags (good).
Content is not escaped, so a page containing </untrusted_web_content> can close the wrapper.
Containment relies on the model obeying the prompt.
No egress limit or gate contains a followed injection that sends data to an attacker URL.

findings.summary: Data and instructions are separated by role and tags, but no code-level control stops a followed injection from exfiltrating through fetch_page or the rendered brief.
findings.next_step: Escape or strip the closing tag in tool output, add containment from B05/B09/R03, write repeated and adaptive injection tests, and run recipe R02.

evidence.note: img is an allowed tag.
img src allowed for any http/https URL.
bleach keeps external images, so the browser fetches attacker URLs when the brief is shown.
str(exc) from tool errors written to the audit log unredacted.

findings.summary: A brief containing a Markdown image pointing at an attacker URL leaks data from the user's browser with no tool call.
findings.next_step: Remove img from ALLOWED_TAGS or limit src to an approved host list, add a CSP img-src policy on the UI, redact exception text, and run the marker test in recipe R03.

evidence.note: Halt flag checked before every model call.
Halt flag checked before every tool call.
Unreadable flag is treated as stop (fail closed).
Flag is a ConfigMap mounted read-only; the ServiceAccount has no token mounted.
Names who may stop it (platform on-call) and how.

findings.summary: An operator-only flag outside the agent's control stops new model and tool calls; in-flight calls are not canceled and ConfigMap updates reach the pod with a kubelet sync delay.
findings.next_step: Set a maximum stop time that includes ConfigMap propagation and the 20s fetch timeout, then run a dated drill per recipe R11 on the current deployment.

evidence.note: Only side effects are HTTP GETs; no writes.
No retries in tool clients.
Runs are synchronous per request; no queues or background jobs.

findings.summary: No writes, queues, or retries exist, so a stop leaves no pending work; outbound GETs already sent cannot be recalled.
findings.next_step: Write down that each operation is a read-only GET that cannot be canceled once sent, and run recipe R12 stopping a run mid-tool-call.
